extracted.intended_audience: K–12 teachers, curriculum specialists, and education researchers involved in implementing or evaluating the 6+1 Trait Writing model (especially grade 5 teachers and district coordinators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and study-design standards for implementing the 6+1 Trait Writing instructional model in K–12 classrooms and for evaluating its effectiveness in a randomized trial. Emphasizes instructional components, professional development dosage, eligibility, and rigorous evaluation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourages collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourages collaboration in planning, drafting, revising, and editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports collaborative practices across all stages of the writing process (planning, drafting, revising, editing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific product goals and trait-based self-assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigns specific goals for writing and then, using trait rubrics, helps students routinely self-assess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers set concrete product goals and use the 6+1 trait rubrics to guide student self-assessment and progress monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word processing (technology use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word processing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a component of instruction, teachers encourage students to use word processing tools to compose and revise; ties to broader guidance encouraging appropriate technology to support development and publication of compositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence combining
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence combining
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaches students to understand and construct more complex, sophisticated sentences by combining, rearranging, expanding, and imitating sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prewriting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages students to generate, gather, and organize ideas for their compositions before writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiry activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages students to organize and analyze information to develop content for their writing—supports research-based content development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process writing approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Process writing approach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes instructional activities appropriate for a process writing workshop environment; graphic overviews show how the model works with the writing process (i.e., supports drafting, revising, editing as iterative steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of models (mentor texts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study of models
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages students to read and analyze models of good writing using the writing traits, focusing on particular audiences, purposes (modes), and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing-content integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing content learning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrates writing with content in other subjects so writing supports and is supported by content-area learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate technology for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourages the use of appropriate technology to support students in the development and publication of compositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond basic word processing, recommend using technology tools that help students develop, revise, and publish finished writing products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multisite cluster randomized trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: A multisite cluster randomized trial was used: schools (not individual students) were randomly assigned to treatment and control to follow implementation recommendations that the intervention be schoolwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cluster randomization aligns with the intended schoolwide implementation and professional development structure; randomization was performed within districts and paired by free/reduced-price lunch rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development dosage and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional development offered included a three-day summer institute and three one-day workshops during the school year, plus online support resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD intensity and format are specified as part of the intervention; the report notes that smaller PD doses in prior studies may have limited their effectiveness and that teachers requested more training/time to implement the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent randomization
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomization of schools to experimental condition was performed by an independent contractor with no specific knowledge of the schools or districts involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an external party for assignment to prevent bias in the randomization process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masking of essay origin for scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Student essays were transmitted to an independent research firm which masked the origin of the essays and assigned new IDs before sending copies for scoring; raters did not know whether essays were pretest/posttest or treatment/control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masking reduces scorer bias; maintained by relabeling and independent handling of essays prior to scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and external verification of data manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All subsequent manipulations of the data file (for example, data cleaning and further data coding) were carefully documented and verified by another external research firm prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and independent verification ensure transparency and guard against undocumented changes to data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted-use data file for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: A restricted-use data file was prepared and can be used by other researchers to replicate the analyses or conduct additional analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a restricted dataset supports replication while preserving confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random assignment stratified/paired by socio-economic indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Within districts, schools were paired based on the proportion of students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch and then one of each pair was randomly assigned to treatment or control (with special handling when odd numbers of schools participated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairing/stratification helps balance socio-economic status across conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power analysis and minimum detectable effect size
rubrics_metrics.description: A statistical power analysis estimated the number of schools/students needed to detect a minimum treatment effect size; minimum detectable effect size targeted ~0.25 SD (final sample yielded ~0.23 SD detectable with 80% power).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power analysis based on prior assessment data guides sample-size decisions to ensure adequate sensitivity for detecting meaningful effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: School eligibility criteria for study participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility required: (1) no recent use of trait-based approaches (no training within previous three years), (2) at least one grade 5 teacher willing to participate and supportive principal, and (3) at least 20 grade 5 students available for participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen districts/schools for prior exposure and logistical feasibility to preserve internal validity and sample stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment, consent, and memoranda of understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Principals signed memoranda of understanding detailing conditions of participation (random assignment, required teacher PD for treatment schools, implementation expectations, and data collection). Contracts with districts specified assistance and remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal agreements clarify expectations and responsibilities and help ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining integrity and tracking attrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining integrity of assignment and tracking differential attrition were emphasized; a CONSORT-style flowchart reported numbers of schools/teachers/students at each phase, and procedures for inclusion/exclusion of students were specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT-like reporting and explicit inclusion rules (e.g., inclusion of all students present at pretest, handling ineligible records) to document sample flow and attrition.
